subtopics.title: Meeting the Graph — Axes, Lines and the Story They Tell

questions.question: What should you always read FIRST on any graph?
options: The axes — their titles, units and scale
The steepest line
The intersection point
The colours of the lines

questions.question: Option B's line starts at R150 on the vertical axis. This intercept represents:
options: The price per unit
The fixed monthly charge paid even at zero usage
The break-even point
The maximum monthly cost

questions.question: Why does Option A's line start at the origin?
options: Because all graphs must start at zero
Because the scale begins at zero
Because Option A has no fixed charge — zero usage costs zero rand
Because Option A is cheaper overall

questions.question: In this tariff graph, the gradient of each line represents:
options: The fixed monthly charge
The price per kilowatt-hour — how much cost rises per extra unit
The total monthly bill
The number of appliances used

questions.question: Option A's line is steeper than Option B's because:
options: A has a bigger fixed charge
A is drawn first
B has a bigger fixed charge
A charges R2,00 per unit while B charges only R1,50 per unit

questions.question: On Option A's line the cost climbs from R200 at 100 kWh to R400 at 200 kWh. The gradient is:
options: R200 per kWh
R2,00 per kWh — a rise of R200 over 100 units
R0,50 per kWh
R4,00 per kWh

questions.question: The break-even point on this graph is at:
options: 150 kWh, where both options cost R300
300 kWh, where both options cost R600
450 kWh, where both options cost R825
0 kWh, where both options cost R150

questions.question: How is the break-even reading verified by calculation?
options: 300 × R2,00 = R600 for A, and R150 + 300 × R1,50 = R600 for B — both equal
R150 + R2,00 = R152 for both
600 ÷ 2 = 300 for both
It cannot be verified without the municipality's data

questions.question: For usage BELOW 300 kWh, which option is cheaper and why?
options: Option B — cheaper units always win
Option A — its line runs below B's, since light users avoid the R150 fixed charge
Both cost the same at all usages below 300
Option B — the fixed charge is refunded

questions.question: What does the break-even point mean for a decision-maker?
options: The cheapest possible bill
The maximum usage allowed
The usage at which both options cost the same — the point of indifference between them
The point where electricity becomes free

subtopics.title: Answering the 450 kWh Question — and the Exam Method

questions.question: At 450 kWh, the costs are:
options: A: R900; B: R825 — Option B is cheaper by R75
A: R825; B: R900 — Option A is cheaper by R75
Both cost R900

questions.question: Without calculating, how does zone logic answer the 450 kWh question?
options: 450 is a big number, so the steeper line wins
450 lies left of break-even, so A wins
The question cannot be answered without calculation
450 lies to the right of the 300 kWh break-even, and beyond break-even the fixed-charge option (B) is cheaper

questions.question: Why should a comparison answer state the rand difference, not just the winner?
options: Because the difference changes the winner
Full marks for comparisons require showing both values and the saving (R75)
It is optional decoration
To make the answer longer

questions.question: Which sense-check confirms the overall picture?
options: Electricity should always get cheaper as you use more
The lines should never cross on a real graph
Heavy users benefiting from the fixed-charge option makes sense, since cheap units reward bulk usage
Zero usage should cost the same on both options

subtopics.title: Two Ways to Pay — the Day Pass and the Membership

questions.question: In the gym comparison, which electricity option plays the part of the 'membership with a joining fee'?
options: Option A — R2,00 per unit, nothing up front
Option B — R150 up front, then R1,50 per unit
Neither, because electricity has no joining fee
Both, equally

questions.question: A household on Option B uses no electricity at all in a month. Its bill is:
options: R0

questions.question: If a tariff graph has no labels, how do you tell which line is which?
options: Ask what each option costs at zero usage, and match that rand amount to where each line starts
The top line is always the expensive one
The longer line is always the fixed-charge one
You cannot tell without the labels

questions.question: Why does neither tariff line ever slope downwards?
options: Because graphs are always drawn upwards
Because your bill never gets smaller when you use more electricity
Because the municipality forbids it
Because the axes start at zero

questions.question: On a cost graph, how steeply a line climbs tells you:
options: How long the contract lasts
How much one more unit costs you
The total bill for the month
The fixed charge

questions.question: A bill rises from R200 at 100 units to R400 at 200 units. The price of one unit is:
Which answer would earn full marks for 'explain what the steeper line means'?
options: It goes up faster than the other one
Option A costs R2,00 per kilowatt-hour against Option B's R1,50, so A's bill rises faster per extra unit
It is the more popular option
It has a bigger fixed charge

questions.question: Two numbers describe a tariff completely. They are:
options: Where the line starts, and how steeply it climbs
The highest and lowest points of the line
The break-even and the total
The month and the meter number

subtopics.title: Where the Lines Swap Places — and the 450-Unit Answer

questions.question: Option B saves you 50c per unit but costs R150 up front. How many units must you use to make that R150 back?
options: 75 units
150 units
300 units
450 units

questions.question: A household using only 180 units a month should choose:
options: Option A, because it never makes back the R150 joining fee
Option B, because cheaper units always win
Either — they cost the same
Option B, because the fixed fee is refunded

questions.question: At 450 units, the saving of 50c on each unit comes to R225, and the fee paid was R150. The household is ahead by:
Which answer to 'which option is cheaper at 450 kWh?' collects all the marks?
options: Option B
Option B, because 450 is past break-even
A costs R900, B costs R825, so Option B is cheaper by R75
B, by quite a lot
